* Fix silently dropped bibtex citations across the book (#136) (#442)

sphinxcontrib-bibtex aborts parsing a .bib file the moment it
encounters a key already registered from an earlier file, silently
dropping every entry below the duplicate. The user-visible symptom on
the deconvolution chapter was empty `[]` brackets for MuSiC, dtangle,
and DWLS — those entries sit below `Schulte-Schrepping2020` in
`bulk_deconvolution.bib`, the same key also lives in
`conditions/differential_gene_expression.bib`, and DGE loads first.
The same pattern was silently hiding entries in five other files.

Resolved by adopting the chapter-prefix convention already used
throughout the book consistently across every registered .bib file
(`at:`, `pa:`, `raw:`, `qc:`, `norm:`, `clust:`, `intg:`, `lt:`, `pt:`,
`de:`, `comp:`, `gspa:`, `pemo:`, `ccc:`, `grn:`, `bd:`, `atac:`,
`sp:`, `air:`, `pi:`, `ai:`, `spat:`, `velo:`, `rsc:`, `dr:`, `fs:`,
`anno:`, `adv:`, `scrna:`, `atacqc:`, `ol:`). Every previously
unprefixed entry was renamed to carry its chapter prefix, every
`{cite}`/`{cite:t}`/`{cite:p}` reference across notebooks and markdown
was updated to match, and same-paper duplicates across chapter bibs
were collapsed onto a single canonical entry.

Also fixes three orphan cites whose entries lived only in the
unregistered `jupyter-book/references.bib`: `osca` and `Amezquita2020`
moved into `introduction/prior_art.bib` with the `pa:` prefix and the
`prior_art.md` cites updated; `Sun2021` cite in
`surface_protein/doublet_detection.ipynb` fixed to `sp:Sun2021`. Drops
a stale `introduction/data_structures_and_frameworks_advanced.bib`
entry from `_config.yml` that pointed at a non-existent file.

A full `jupyter-book build .` after these changes reports zero
"could not find bibtex key", zero "repeated bibliograhpy entry", and
zero "duplicate label" warnings. The bug-report paragraph now renders
all four cites:

  Examples of such tools are CIBERSORTx [Newman et al., 2019], MuSiC
  [Wang et al., 2019], dtangle [Hunt et al., 2018] and DWLS
  [Tsoucas et al., 2019].

* Expand the whole table of contents in the sidebar (#468)

The book theme opens only the section holding the current page and leaves
the other fourteen collapsed, so a reader who does not already know which
part a chapter lives in has to open the sections one by one. The Sphinx
build of this book never asked that.

The theme has no option for it, and the sections are Radix collapsibles
that do not render their children while closed, so CSS cannot reveal them
either. They are opened the way a reader would, from the theme's client
entry bundle, and the sidebar is scrolled to the chapter being read, which
in a list this long is otherwise below the fold.

The rows are tightened to match: the theme sizes them for a mostly
collapsed tree, which makes the full list far taller than it needs to be.

The bundle patching is shared with the back button workaround rather than
repeated.

* Fix the release workflow and refresh the GitHub Actions (#470)

* Fix the release workflow and refresh the GitHub Actions

publish_book.yml had drifted away from build_book.yml: it pinned Python 3.13, installed with pip instead of uv, and pinned jupytext and beautifulsoup4 to versions CI never exercises.
The release therefore ran a configuration no CI run had validated.
It now matches build_book.yml exactly, so what CI proves on main is what gets deployed.

The jupyter-cache step never did anything.
Notebooks are not executed during the build (only jupyter-book, jupytext and beautifulsoup4 are installed), so jupyter-book/_build/.jupyter_cache is never created and every run ends in "Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist, hence no cache is being saved".
Its key also hashed notebook_scripts/**/*.py, a directory that does not exist, and fell back to refs/heads/master.
Removed from both workflows.

The pdfhtml job had been green while producing nothing: latexmk is not on the runner, so myst exported the TeX and then failed to render, and the artifact upload only warned that no file was found.
Install a TeX distribution and set if-no-files-found to error, so a broken export fails the job instead of passing silently.

Also drop the PREVIEW_BRANCH env left behind when the PR preview was removed in #427, drop the non-existent master branch from the labeler trigger, and bring checkout, setup-python, release-drafter and the labeler action up to their current major versions.
The two jobs that gained an explicit permissions block have every scope they need declared, since unlisted scopes drop to none once a block exists.

* Stop presenting an underflowed p-value as a p-value of zero (#477)

The chapter introduced two genes as having corrected p-values of 0.0, which a p-value cannot be.
Squidpy computes them analytically under a normality assumption, and for these genes the result is smaller than the smallest positive double, so the table shows the underflow rather than the value.

The text now says so, and points at n_perms as the alternative, where the number of permutations bounds how small a reported p-value can get.

* Explain the negative binomial in the scRNA-seq chapter (#478)

The chapter stated that transcription is modelled with a negative binomial and that it captures overdispersion, without saying why a Poisson does not do.
The dropdown gives the reason, the gamma mixture that produces the distribution, and a worked example of the spread a dispersion parameter has to absorb.

* Hide noisy cell output and explain five core concepts (#479)

Session info dumps, R console chatter, progress bars, training logs, download logs and deprecation warnings ran to hundreds of lines in places, pushing the content of a chapter off the screen.
58 such cells across 21 notebooks are tagged hide-output, which puts the output behind a toggle rather than removing it.
Cells whose noise wraps a real result are left alone, since the tag hides everything a cell emits, and plots are untouched throughout.
One cell had spelled the tag hide_output, which jupyter-book does not recognise.

Five chapters named a core concept and moved on, so each gains a dropdown: deviance in feature selection, why ADT counts are compositional, the mixture model behind bulk deconvolution, what unspliced counts contribute to RNA velocity, and what the neighborhood enrichment permutation test holds fixed.

Signed-off-by: Lukas Heumos <lukas.heumos@posteo.net>

* Ship the sidebar expanded instead of expanding it after load (#482)

Every section of the table of contents was opened by clicking its chevron from a script appended to the client bundle, which can only run once the page is up.

to keep memory low).

The chapter assigns guides (matching the published calls for every
cell), identifies perturbed cells with Mixscape and validates them with
PD-L1 protein, tests differential expression on replicate pseudobulks
with PyDESeq2, quantifies and tests perturbation effects with the
E-distance and E-test, and clusters the 200 strongest perturbations,
which recovers ribosomal, spliceosome, exosome, proteasome, Mediator,
Integrator, PAF1 and tRNA-synthetase/ISR modules.
Response prediction is covered in prose only: recent independent
benchmarks (Ahlmann-Eltze 2025, Csendes 2025, Kernfeld 2025, Wei 2026,

simple baselines, so running scGen as a best-practice example would
mislead.

multi-sample condition data rather than screens.
pertpy's nearest_perturbations fails when a neighbor graph already

chapter uses leiden clusters and a table instead.

* Rewrite the multimodal integration chapters in Python with public data

Both chapters loaded their data from personal cluster paths, ran WNN
and bridge integration through R, scored methods with the deprecated
scib package, used multigrate from a git branch, and could not be
reproduced by readers.
They now run end to end in one Python environment on the NeurIPS 2021
bone marrow CITE-seq and Multiome data, which
scripts/multimodal_integration uploads from GEO (GSE194122) to lamindb
together with the GENCODE v41 GTF that GLUE needs.

Method choices follow the independent benchmarks of Hu 2024, Fu 2025
and Liu 2025 (Nature Methods): WNN via muon as the paired baseline,
totalVI for CITE-seq, MultiVI for Multiome and mosaic data, GLUE for
unpaired RNA and ATAC, and totalVI with scArches surgery for reference
mapping.
MOFA+ stays for its interpretable factors.
Embeddings are scored with scib-metrics (BRAS instead of silhouette
batch) against the unimodal embeddings, which makes the gain of each
method visible.
The advanced chapter holds out a modality or part of the data in every
example, so GLUE's label transfer (82% lineage, 63% fine types),
totalVI's protein imputation (median Spearman 0.37) and the incomplete
dataset mixing of mosaic MultiVI are all checked against measurements.

multigrate was dropped: 1.0.1 fails with anndata 0.13, and after
pinning anndata 0.12 it did not mix the CITE-seq and Multiome cells at
all in this setting, while MultiVI covers the same trimodal case.
Seurat bridge integration, MIDAS and StabMap are mentioned with their
benchmark results but not run, since bridge is R-only and MIDAS pins
anndata < 0.13 and mudata < 0.4.
pandas is pinned to 2.3 because scglue 0.4.1 writes into a read-only
array under pandas 3 copy-on-write.

The per-chapter environments are replaced by one section environment.

Closes #208 items "Multimodal paired" and "Multimodal advanced".

* Drop the pandas pin from the multimodal environment and silence warnings

scglue 0.4.1 divides a read-only Series.to_numpy() result in place in
estimate_balancing_weight, which fails under pandas 3 copy-on-write
(reported as gao-lab/GLUE#140). Instead of pinning pandas < 3, the GLUE
fit patches Series.to_numpy to return a copy for the duration of the
call, which keeps the balancing step. Skipping balancing instead lowered
label transfer from 82% to 76% (lineage) and from 63% to 58% (fine).

The ADT matrix is converted to CSC before CLR, warnings are filtered
before the imports as in the surface protein chapters, and the jax
logger is set to ERROR to drop the CUDA jaxlib message. Both chapters
were rerun under pandas 3.0.6; GLUE fine-level accuracy is now 64% and
the median totalVI protein correlation 0.34.
